title: Austin Dairy Rules & Street Safety Debate
summary:
• **Dairy regulations debated:** The Council adopted new health rules for dairy operations, but rejected a controversial requirement for cheesecloth over milk vessels; heated debate included testimony from local dairymen concerned about practicality.

• **Water infrastructure expansion requested:** Citizens petitioned to extend water mains to Chicon Street on 3rd Street, with the request referred to the Water & Light Commission.

• **Several financial claims settled:** The Council approved refunds and settlement payments for overpaid pound fees, property damages, and tax corrections from various citizens.

• **Pound yard expansion tabled:** A contentious proposal to extend pound limits in the 7th Ward—with 171 petition signatures—was sent to a special committee after debate, rather than being immediately approved or rejected.

• **Street safety improvements ordered:** The Council directed work on Shoal Creek Road (where fences made it dangerously narrow) and Oakwood Avenue (where water drainage was flooding a resident's basement).

Alderman Armstrong offered the following resolution : Whereas Mr George Freund has built a
fence cutting off the old road along Shoal creek so much that two wagons cannot pass each
other for some distance making it quite a dangerous place, and Whereas the Messrs Theile
have built a barb wire fence along the other side of said road making it still more
dangerous in case a horse becomes frightened ; Therefore be it resolved that the Street
